svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Put on an event · fill the lineup · sell or give away tickets · scan people in. Hosting needs Organizer $10/mo; charging for tickets needs a connected bank.

g.text: Fill in the form
Title, date, time, place, and how many people
can come (leave it blank for unlimited).
Or photograph the flyer
AI reads the poster and fills the form in for you.
You check it before it goes live.
OpenAI vision
Or we already found it
Around 800 events pulled nightly from SF
calendars, libraries and venues.
scraped sources · no work from you
The event page
One public page carrying the lineup, the map pin, the ticket box and the photo wall. It shows up in the community feed, on the map, and on every business page in the lineup.
Build the lineup
Search local businesses, tick several, invite them
all at once. Their role — food, performer, sponsor,
volunteer — is worked out from what they are.
Accepted businesses show grouped by role on
the public page.
Or they join themselves
Print the event's QR code and put it on the table.
A business already with us asks to join and you
approve. One that isn't gets interviewed by the
AI on their phone and a profile is built from
the conversation.
Tell everyone at once
One message to the whole accepted lineup.
Group chat
Email · Resend
Text message
Everyone invited also gets a phone notification
and an email, so nothing is missed.
Free — just RSVP
They tap Going and say how many are coming.
A free event still issues real scannable tickets,
so the door works exactly the same way as it
does at a paid one.
no card, no bank account needed
Paid — set your tiers
Early bird, general, VIP — each with its own price,
how many exist, and when sales stop.
Buyers need no account — email only. Money goes
to your bank, platform keeps 5%.
same bank connection as the shop · Stripe
Scan them in at the door
Open the scanner on your phone. Point it at their
QR — green, and they're in.
A second scan is refused, showing when that ticket
already came in — so a screenshot passed to a
friend doesn't get anybody through twice.

svg.text: A party of four arrives as four separate tickets, because the door counts people, not receipts.
Refund someone and their ticket stops scanning. Your attendee list, capacity and blasts all keep working the same whether tickets were free or paid.
Every business you put on the lineup sees the event on their own dashboard, with the role they agreed to turn up as.
